question: Which current public evaluations, speed and price measurements are trustworthy and current enough to set the default model for each of the tiers fast, balanced, quality and best, for the models of the providers the hub can call?
decision: adopt public evaluations as each tier's default metric input, with the hub's own measurement as a later override
method: Fix the tiers' uses and the rule 'independent first, vendor-reported graded lower, a model with no number is not eligible' before reading numbers; open each leaderboard page; read the numbers from the page data; grade each source; write the weights before computing a ranking.
criteria: Included: independent runs under one setting that cover the current models of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek, dated November 2026, readable without a login. Excluded: vendor-reported tables, boards not updated since before the current models, pages not readable.
sources: web search; opened pages (Artificial Analysis leaderboard and methodology, Vals AI index and sub-boards, vendor price pages, Scale, Berkeley function calling, METR, Epoch, OpenRouter)
queries: web search | Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index current models November 2026 | 2026-11-10 | 17; opened | artificialanalysis.ai leaderboard | 2026-11-10 | 1; opened | artificialanalysis.ai methodology | 2026-11-10 | 1; opened | vals.ai benchmarks, vals index, science index, terminal bench 4, swebench, programbench | 2026-11-10 | 6; opened | vendor pricing pages (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek) | 2026-11-10 | 4; opened | labs.scale.com, gorilla.cs.berkeley.edu, metr.org, epoch.ai, openrouter.ai, llm-stats.com, tbench.ai, arena.ai, livebench.ai | 2026-11-10 | 9
screened_out: 3 not readable without scripts or blocked (LMArena, LiveBench, Terminal-Bench 4.1 board); 1 page missing (tau3 post); 1 older than the models (Berkeley function calling board, updated 2026-04-12); 1 no longer updated (METR); 1 measures usage, not quality (OpenRouter); 1 human check blocked (llm-stats); 1 opened but the board rows are not in the page (SWE-bench Pro public)
stop: the sources opened today cover every candidate model on one independent board and a second board cross-checks it
synthesis_known: Artificial Analysis publishes, per model and reasoning effort, nine index evaluations, cost per task, time per task, speed and price for every current Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek model, under identical settings; the Vals Index (2026-11-09) ranks the same models with its own cost and latency. Gemini 3.6 Flash is deprecated, so the hub's older candidate list was out of date.
synthesis_contested: The two boards order the mid models differently (Vals puts Claude Sonnet 5.5 above GPT-6.1 Sol; Artificial Analysis capability puts them close); cost per task is long agentic work, not one short call; Gemini 4 Carbon has a promotional price until 2026-11-30.
synthesis_unknown: No current public evaluation covers classification or extraction (IFBench has no rows for current models); the tool-use board (BFCL) and SWE-bench Pro rows for current models were not read; the writing leaderboard (LMArena) was blocked; whether the hub's callers pass a reasoning effort is not verified.
limitations: One aggregator supplies every scored number (grade B at most); the Vals board is a cross-check only; the research ran at the standard size with fewer than the five source kinds a full review needs; no numbers were read from a vendor-reported table.
decisions: Artificial Analysis index evaluations: adopt: independent, current, covers every candidate; Vals Index: adapt: cross-check only, one number per model; SWE-bench Pro: defer: board rows not read; BFCL: reject: not updated since before the current models; LMArena: defer: blocked; METR: reject: no longer updated

question: Which public evaluations speak to each kind of model call (classify, gather, orchestrate, work, review, write, structure), directly or by proxy, so that the tier a call role uses rests on public numbers and not on the owner's preference alone?
decision: adopt the evaluations recorded in role_tier_metrics.csv as the evidence for each role's tier, with the owner's hard constraints applied after the metric
method: Fix the rule before computing any role: for each kind the evaluations that speak to it with a weight and a direct or proxy mark, one ladder, the base gain, the frequency and stakes factors and the price premium, all written in role_tier_metrics.csv; read only the public numbers already in the registry (no new lookup); compute the table once; if the rule looks wrong say so and do not retune.
criteria: Included: evaluations of the independent board already read on 2026-11-10 (tier_public_scores.csv) and the list prices in tier_prices.csv, for the models that fill the four tiers. Excluded: any number not in the registry, vendor-reported tables, our own case sets as a decider (they stay as a note on a row).
sources: the hub registry files tier_public_scores.csv and tier_prices.csv (public rows checked 2026-11-10); the earlier review inv-2026-11-10-tier-public-evaluations for the grade of each evaluation
queries: opened | registry/tier_public_scores.csv | 2026-11-11 | 12; opened | registry/tier_prices.csv | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | recorded Claude Code session usage on this machine (aggregates only, no text) | 2026-11-11 | 1373
screened_out: 2 not used by any kind of call (terminal_bench_science, which speaks to no role kind, and the composite index, which only the best tier uses and the metric never reaches)
synthesis_known: Nine public evaluations of one independent board speak to the kinds of call, directly for tool and workflow completion, non-hallucination, agentic and long-horizon work, repository changes and expert-judged work products, by proxy for expert reasoning and for classification (no public evaluation measures classification on current models). All nine and the list prices are dated 2026-11-10, one day old on the day of the computation and inside the 45 day limit.
synthesis_contested: On the numbers, the balanced tier's model does not beat the fast tier's on non-hallucination (the fast tier's model scores higher) while it beats it on tool completion, agentic and expert reasoning evaluations, so the kind's weights decide the gap; the quality tier's model leads the balanced tier's on agentic, coding and expert reasoning evaluations by a modest margin at about twice the list price and is at a different default reasoning effort, which one board cannot separate.
synthesis_unknown: No public evaluation measures reviewing, orchestrating or classifying on current models, so those kinds rest on proxies; one aggregator supplies every number (grade B at most); the evaluations publish no interval, so the base gain is twice the existing 5 percent tolerance and is a choice, not a measurement; the frequency, stakes and volume class of each role is read from its call path and is the owner's to confirm; tokens per call are measured for the deep-work roles (median of 1373 recorded sessions, one machine, all kinds of work) and from small evaluation cases for six roles and estimated for the rest; the cache price multipliers (0.1 for reads, 1.25 for writes) are taken from the vendor's public pricing page as recorded in the price registry and were not re-opened today; the dollar values of a full gain and the cost weight are assumptions with their sensitivity recorded in the metric; the rule was revised once on the owner's instruction after the first table was seen (recorded in role_tier_metrics.csv).
limitations: Quick size, the registry only: no new lookup, so every item is marked not-opened today and carries the grade of the earlier review; the numbers are one day old and must be refreshed by 2026-12-25 (the freshness limit), after which the table is recomputed and any stale row says so.
decisions: Public evaluations per kind in role_tier_metrics.csv: adopt: the nine evaluations speak to the kinds as recorded; List prices for the price premium: adopt: the same price rows the tier choice uses; Own case sets as the decider of a tier: reject: the owner holds that public evaluations suffice and own cases stay a note; Vals Index: defer: one number per model with no split by kind

question: How should a terminal arm be measured on how its screen is drawn, with public sources that can be checked, and may a model judge it?
decision: adopt a deterministic layer 1 (named checks over an emulated screen) as the ranking number after the correctness gate; adopt a model-judged layer 2 as advisory only, built and calibrated but not run on any arm; adopt the Agent Client Protocol with an external terminal client as a separate arm
method: Fix the checks, their bounds and their weights before any arm is scored; open each published source and read the claim from the page; install the external client in a scratch folder and read its own help for the launch form; write down what a model-judged review is known to miss before building one.
criteria: Included: the protocol specification, the licence of every library the metric or the arm would import or launch, the published guidelines the layer 2 checklist is drawn from, and published studies of model-judged usability evaluation. Excluded: vendor marketing pages and any claim about a terminal client that was not read in its own repository or help output.
sources: opened pages and package metadata; ran the client's own help in a scratch install
queries: opened | https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16345 | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02306 | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/overview | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://github.com/batrachianai/toad | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://pypi.org/project/pyte/ | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://pypi.org/project/agent-client-protocol/ | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://clig.dev/ | 2026-11-11 | 1; opened | https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/articles/guidelines-for-human-ai-interaction-eighteen-best-practices-for-human-centered-ai-design/ | 2026-11-11 | 1; ran | toad acp --help in a scratch install | 2026-11-11 | 1
synthesis_known: Two published studies of model-judged usability evaluation disagree on how much a model finds: one measured that GPT-4o found 21.2% of the issues experts found with false positives from speculation (arXiv 2506.16345), the other that a multimodal model found 73% and 77% of the issues across two apps, more than five experienced evaluators (arXiv 2507.02306). Both agree it is weaker on interaction conventions and on problems that span screens. The Agent Client Protocol is JSON-RPC 2.0 with an agent run as a subprocess of the client, sessions, prompts, cancellation, permission requests and extension by underscore methods. Toad is AGPL-3.0, is run as its own program and launches an agent from a command (`toad acp COMMAND PATH`). pyte is LGPL-3.0 and the Python SDK for the protocol is Apache-2.0 by its packaged licence file.
synthesis_contested: The studies disagree on direction, so neither supports trusting a model to judge a terminal screen: both measured screens of graphical apps (not text grids), with different models, prompts and expert panels; whether a judge on a text frame with a quoted-evidence rule does better is not known until it is calibrated.
synthesis_unknown: How a model judge behaves on text grids of terminal screens; how the external client draws a hub session beyond one scripted launch; whether Toad's terminal rendering can be captured by the same emulator without a person (one launch was tried); the contrast a terminal really draws for faint text (it varies by terminal).
limitations: Both studies are abstracts read on 2026-11-11 (the papers were not read in full), on graphical apps. The SDK's licence is not stated on its PyPI page and was read from the LICENSE file in the installed wheel. WCAG success criterion 1.4.3 (4.5:1) is cited from the standard and was not opened today. pyte has had no release since November 2023. Layer 2 was built and its calibration set frozen but not run on any arm, by decision: a live arm is never run just to fill a row.
decisions: Layer 1 deterministic metric: adopt: the emulated screen is free, repeatable and reads what the person sees; Layer 2 model-judged review: adopt as advisory only: the published evidence is mixed and from other kinds of screen, so it is measured on injected defects first and never gates; pyte for evaluation only: adopt: LGPL-3.0, imported by the evaluation folder and never by the hub package; Toad: adopt as a separate arm run as its own program: AGPL-3.0 allows it only that way; Agent Client Protocol SDK: adopt as an optional extra: Apache-2.0
